EMYRGEN GROUP · KINGDOM OF SAUDI ARABIA

From environmental intelligence to measurable action.

An integrated national capability for water security, the Saudi Green Initiative, environmental resilience and autonomous environmental operations.

EMYRGEN proposes to connect environmental observations, decision support, three complementary autonomous aviation classes, authorized field activities and measurable results under Saudi governance.

Explore the national program ↓See the six Saudi intelligence layers ↓

01 / National opportunity

A national environmental mission, built around Saudi priorities.

Water scarcity, vegetation survival, exposed terrain and remote field access require better operational information—not isolated aerial images.

The program is designed to bring climate intelligence closer to the decisions and field work that influence environmental outcomes.

  • Water securityUnderstand irrigation conditions and measure water use against restoration success.
  • Saudi Green InitiativeIdentify establishment problems early and verify tree and vegetation outcomes over time.
  • ResilienceSupport dust-source awareness, atmospheric research and protection of strategic infrastructure.
  • Autonomous field operationsConnect environmental findings to approved inspection, equipment delivery and follow-up missions.

02 / The EMYRGEN aviation ecosystem

Three aircraft classes. One coordinated mission architecture.

Precision. Regional intelligence. Heavy unmanned operations. Each capability serves a distinct purpose within one national program.

Aircraft class 01 / Precision

Local inspection, tree health and site-level intelligence.

The EGX-10 is the precision inspection platform for targeted vegetation imaging, planting-site assessment and verified follow-up.

  • Reference payload: 10 kg class
  • Mission focus: localized sensing, rapid inspections and precision evidence collection

Aircraft class 02 / Regional intelligence

Extended-area environmental monitoring and scientific missions.

The EGX-200 supports the wider operational picture through regional surveys, advanced sensor integration and atmospheric observation mission profiles.

  • Program reference: 200 kg payload and up to six-hour endurance, configuration dependent
  • Mission focus: regional environmental intelligence, scientific payloads and survey operations

Aircraft class 03 / Autonomous conversion

Transform existing manned helicopters into unmanned operational assets.

EMYRGEN’s helicopter-to-UAS conversion technology can be applied to suitable conventional airframes, subject to integration, approvals and airframe-specific validation.

  • Technology: autonomous conversion, avionics and flight-control integration
  • Saudi applications: equipment transport, difficult-access field support and logistics
  • Heavy-lift target: selected configurations in a proposed 1,000–3,000 kg class

03 / Water intelligence

Every drop deserves better information.

Saudi water operations can benefit from targeted sensing that links soil condition, irrigation demand, restoration status and field response.

The proposed system prioritizes validated observations before intervention and connects water-management decisions to measurable survival and efficiency outcomes.

  • Soil and irrigation screeningCombine available satellite indicators and ground observations with appropriately integrated aerial sensing.
  • Prioritized inspectionsDirect EGX-10 and EGX-200 missions to sites where early investigation can improve decisions.
  • Measurable effectivenessTrack water consumed per surviving tree and adjust irrigation plans based on evidence.

04 / Saudi Green Initiative

Protect the investment behind every planted tree.

A national restoration program succeeds through establishment, survival and long-term land stewardship—not planting totals alone.

The EMYRGEN mission network would help Saudi operators prioritize inspections, assess vegetation condition and review restoration outcomes across seasons.

  • ObserveScreen planting areas, vegetation corridors and site-level stress indicators.
  • RespondSend the appropriate sensing asset and coordinate a locally authorized field response.
  • VerifyCompare follow-up observations at 6, 12 and 24 months to evaluate environmental progress.

05 / Operation Green Arabia

Six visible stages.
One connected environmental mission.

A proposed Saudi restoration-site workflow links environmental intelligence to authorized field action, measurable results and continuous program improvement.

  1. 01 / SIX-STAGE WORKFLOW

    Detect

    Satellite and available ground observations indicate a possible vegetation or irrigation anomaly requiring review.

  2. 02 / SIX-STAGE WORKFLOW

    Select

    A Saudi operator selects the restoration area and confirms the intended inspection objective and approvals.

  3. 03 / SIX-STAGE WORKFLOW

    Inspect

    An EGX-10 or EGX-200 mission gathers condition-specific sensing and imagery under the approved mission plan.

  4. 04 / SIX-STAGE WORKFLOW

    Assess

    The responsible team reviews evidence, environmental context, constraints and potential causes.

  5. 05 / SIX-STAGE WORKFLOW

    Authorize

    The Saudi authority determines whether to dispatch a field team, adjust irrigation or employ authorized logistics support.

  6. 06 / SIX-STAGE WORKFLOW

    Verify

    Subsequent observations and field records assess results against baseline conditions and program economics.

06 / Environmental operations

Intelligence must connect to action.

Suitably converted unmanned helicopters can extend logistical access to remote restoration, monitoring and infrastructure sites.

The helicopter-to-UAS capability is a technical conversion proposition, not simply a third off-the-shelf aircraft model.

  • Move environmental equipmentDeliver instruments, restoration supplies, pumping components and approved logistical payloads.
  • Support constrained terrainEvaluate airborne delivery where road access, time or ground alternatives make aviation operationally justified.
  • Operate within verified limitsConfirm airframe, temperature, elevation, fuel, payload and regulatory constraints before deployment.

06A / Technology integration

Autonomy engineering. Aircraft conversion. Saudi capability transfer.

Conversion is built around avionics, control-system integration, engineering discipline, validation and maintainable operations—not a cosmetic aircraft modification.

The Saudi partnership can define an industrial and training pathway for locally supported integration, maintenance and mission operations.

07 / Cloud intelligence

Atmospheric research within a national operational system.

Authorized atmospheric missions can supplement Saudi satellite, radar and ground observations through specialized airborne measurement payloads.

Scientific objectives, aircraft performance, permissions and data quality requirements would be established with Saudi research and environmental authorities before field deployment.

08 / Sandstorm & desertification intelligence

Understand sources. Prepare and respond.

A regional airborne sensing layer can support dust-source assessment, exposed-soil monitoring and critical-infrastructure preparedness.

The proposed value is improved awareness, forecasting support and scientifically justified local mitigation—not a claim that autonomous aircraft can stop regional sandstorms.

10 / National impact & Saudi capability

Success should be measured on the ground.

Saudi program value will be assessed through verifiable environmental outcomes, operational efficiency and lasting technical capacity.

The pilot should establish baseline measurements before presenting improvements or economic results.

  • Tree survivalIndependent survival review after 6, 12 and 24 months.
  • Water productivityWater consumed per surviving tree and measurable irrigation efficiency.
  • Response qualityTime from reported anomaly to validated condition assessment.
  • Restoration economicsCost per successfully treated or verified site, not simply number of flights.
  • Saudi technical developmentLocal engineers, analysts, maintainers and mission operators trained.

10 / Saudi technology development · continued

Build and sustain the capability within the Kingdom.

Saudi mission governance, locally developed workforce skills, data stewardship and technical support form part of the long-term value proposition.

Industrial collaboration would address systems integration, maintenance, autonomous operations, environmental analytics and agreed licensing or technology-transfer terms.

  • ControlSaudi-owned mission priorities, operating procedures and authorizations.
  • TalentTraining pathways for operators, aerospace engineers, maintainers and environmental analysts.
  • DataAppropriate Saudi governance of environmental information, reports and decision records.
  • IndustryProgressive localization of aircraft support, integration capability and operations.

11 / Pilot-to-scale implementation

A phased pathway from pilot to national capability.

The initial Saudi engagement should establish scope, responsible stakeholders, operating permissions, mission priorities and the evidence required for national scaling.

The climate workstream should have its own mission requirements, costs and outcome-based approval stages.

0–3 months

Pilot preparation

Select Saudi partners and restoration sites; define measurements, permissions, governance and operational costs.

4–12 months

Water & greening field operations

Conduct approved sensing missions, examine irrigation priorities and evaluate vegetation and restoration outcomes.

Year 2

Conversion logistics & environmental science

Validate helicopter-to-UAS field logistics where justified, then extend atmospheric and dust programs with Saudi institutions.

Year 3+

National scaling

Scale demonstrated applications, local support and technical workforce capability after evidence-based evaluation.

12 / Requested Saudi decision

Establish the joint Saudi–EMYRGEN technical and commercial working group.

Define and launch a Saudi Climate Intelligence Pilot Program beginning with water security, vegetation health and authorized autonomous environmental operations.

The working group would establish the initial mission areas, validate airframe and sensor integration requirements, agree operating and data governance, and define the commercial and environmental results needed to progress toward deployment and localization.
